result:
The proposed answer, 2^2025, is incorrect. The real count is 3^2025, because the solution misreads how bricks in adjacent layers touch.

Take the wall to have a fixed total width. Layer n has a = 2^n − 1 bricks, so brick i occupies [i/a, (i+1)/a]. Layer n+1 has b = 2a + 1 bricks.

Brick i in layer n shares a side with brick j in layer n+1 exactly when their intervals overlap with positive length. That condition gives 2i − 1 + i/a < j < 2i + 2 + (i+1)/a.

For every i from 0 to a − 1, this allows j = 2i, 2i + 1 and 2i + 2. All three indices lie within 0, …, 2a, so every brick has exactly 3 bricks below it that it shares a side with.

Check on the first two layers: the single brick in layer 1 touches all 3 bricks of layer 2. In layer 2, brick 0 spans [0, 1/3] and touches bricks 0, 1 and 2 of layer 3, which span [0, 1/7], [1/7, 2/7] and [2/7, 3/7].

Each move therefore has 3 choices, and Jessica makes 2025 moves to reach layer 2026. The number of move sequences is 3^2025.

The proposed solution assumed each brick touches only 2 bricks below, which gives 2^2025. The final answer shown, a number of about 610 digits, matches 2^2025 in size rather than 3^2025, which has about 966 digits.

VERDICT: REJECT
